question.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(4,-2,3)$ and is  perpendicular to the line 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+2t \\ y=3-2t \\ z=5+t.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨4,-2,3⟩.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+2t \\ y=3-2t \\ z=5+t\end{aligned}\,⇒\,⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨-1,3,5⟩+t\text{ }{{⟨2,-2,1⟩}_{⏟}}_{v}.
$$

   

The direction vector of the line is $v=⟨2,-2,1⟩.$ So, a normal  vector to the plane is 

$$
n=v=⟨2,-2,1⟩.
$$

 

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,-2,1⟩ & =⟨4,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨2,-2,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,-2,1⟩ & =15.\end{aligned}
$$
